dc.description:
The Trendi corpus is a monitor corpus of Slovenian. It contains news articles from 106 media websites, published by 64 publishers. Trendi 2026-07 covers the period from January 2019 to July 2026, complementing the Gigafida 2.2 reference corpus of written Slovene (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/2106).

The contents of the Trendi corpus are obtained using the Jožef Stefan Institute Newsfeed service (http://newsfeed.ijs.si/). The texts have been annotated using the CLASSLA-Stanza pipeline (https://github.com/clarinsi/classla), including syntactic parsing according to the Universal Dependencies (https://universaldependencies.org/sl/) and Named Entities (https://nl.ijs.si/janes/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/SlovenianNER-eng-v1.1.pdf).

An important addition are topics or thematical categories, which have been automatically assigned to each text. There are 13 categories altogether: Arts and culture, Crime and accidents, Economy, Environment, Health, Leisure, Politics and Law, Science and Technology, Society, Sports, Weather, Entertainment, and Education. The text classification uses the following models: Text classification model SloBERTa-Trendi-Topics 1.0 (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1709), Text classification model fastText-Trendi-Topics 1.0 (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1710), and the SloBERTa model (https://huggingface.co/cjvt/sloberta-trendi-topics).

The corpus is currently not available as a downloadable dataset due to copyright restrictions but we hope to make at least some of it available in the near future. The corpus is accessible through CLARIN.SI concordancers. If you would like to use the dataset for research purposes, please contact Iztok Kosem (iztok.kosem@ijs.si).

English-Slovene sample of the ETHICS dataset ETHICS-EN-SL 1.0 contains an English-Slovene sample derived from the ETHICS dataset (Hendrycks et al. 2021), prepared for a master’s thesis on language as a factor in the moral evaluation of large language models. The resource contains selected examples from five ETHICS subsets: commonsense moral judgment, deontology, justice, virtue ethics, and utilitarianism.

The dataset contains 100 examples or scenario pairs per subset. The English files contain the selected examples from the original ETHICS dataset, while the Slovene files contain translated and partially localized versions of the same examples. The bilingual files align the English and Slovene versions row by row. For the Slovene part of the study, a human reference baseline was established on the basis of majority judgments by Slovene annotators.

The resource is intended for research on multilingual moral evaluation, language effects in large language models, value alignment, dataset translation and localization, and the creation of localized evaluation resources for less-resourced languages. The data are distributed as UTF-8 encoded TSV files with header rows. The package also includes a README file with the directory structure and column descriptions.

The resource is based on the ETHICS dataset introduced by Hendrycks et al. (2021): 
Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Steven Basart, Andrew Critch, Jerry Li, Dawn Song, and Jacob Steinhardt. “Aligning AI With Shared Human Values.” ICLR 2021. https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.02275

dc.contributor.author: Chatterjee, Nishan¦Koloski, Boshko¦Doucet, Antoine¦Pollak, Senja¦Purver, Matthew
dc.subject: aspect-based sentiment analysis¦targeted sentiment analysis¦entity-level sentiment analysis¦document-level sentiment analysis¦news corpus¦media monitoring
local.sponsor: Slovenian Research and Innovation Agency (ARIS)@@P2-0103@@Core research program Knowledge Technologies@@nationalFunds@@¦ARRS (Slovenian Research Agency)@@L2-50070@@Embeddings-based techniques for Media Monitoring Applications@@nationalFunds@@¦ARIS (Slovenian Research and Innovation Agency)@@GC-0002@@LLM4DH: Large Language Models for Digital Humanities@@nationalFunds@@¦Young Researcher Grant@@PR-12394@@ARIS@@nationalFunds@@¦Nouvelle-Aquitaine Region, France@@2022-2021-17014610@@ACTUADA@@Other@@¦European Union HORIZON-WIDERA-2023-TALENTS-01-01@@101186647@@EU Era Chair (AI4DH)@@euFunds@@
dc.description:
AspectBench 1.0 (HBS Subset) is an HBS language dataset (hbs, ISO 639-3) containing online news articles, mainly in Serbian and Croatian, for studying sentiment towards target entities like companies and brand names. It is a document-level aspect-based sentiment analysis dataset containing long articles and unseen or new target entities that are not encountered during training. The article text has been filtered to remove URLs.

The dataset contains 82,714 distinct records covering 65 targets. The articles were published between 31 December 2012 and 30 December 2023. The held-out test set contains 12,407 records. The other 70,307 records form one training and validation pool. Three random splits of this pool are provided. Each split contains 57,901 training records and 12,406 validation records. Only the source-system internal identifier was removed. The article text, sentiment labels, aspect names, and aspect tags are unchanged.

Each record is one document-aspect pair. It contains the full article headline and body, one target company or brand, the target's tracked keyword patterns, the number of matched mentions, publication metadata, and one sentiment label: negative (-1), neutral (0), or positive (1). A single article can occur in more than one record when it has more than one target. The literal <aspect>...</aspect> tags in the article mark the mentions that refer to that record's target. These tags are part of the annotation.

Examples:

{
  "uuid": "11855",
  "article": "bankama u srbiji bolje nego ikada ... neke banke poput sosijete zeneral banke i <aspect>erste banke</aspect> pohvalile su se da su postigle najbolji rezultat otkako posluju u srbiji. ...",
  "translation": "Banks in Serbia are doing better than ever ... Some banks, such as Societe Generale Bank and Erste Bank, highlighted that they achieved their best result since they began operating in Serbia. ...",
  "aspect": "Erste banka",
  "keywords": ["erst* bank*", "ерст* банк*"],
  "sentiment": 1,
  "language": "Serbo-Croatian",
  "published": "2017-05-02T22:00:00.000Z",
  "country": "RS"
}

{
  "uuid": "11854",
  "article": "bankama u srbiji bolje nego ikada ... <aspect>telenor banka</aspect> ponovila je los rezultat iz prve godine poslovanja, a strucnjaci kazu da je to ocekivano zbog ogromnih ulaganja i da bi odrzivost ovog modela poslovanja mogla da se oceni posle cetiri, pet godina. ...",
  "translation": "Banks in Serbia are doing better than ever ... Telenor Bank repeated the weak result from its first year of operation, while experts said this was expected because of substantial investments and that the sustainability of this business model could be assessed after four or five years. ...",
  "aspect": "Telenor banka",
  "keywords": ["telenor bank*", "теленор банк*"],
  "sentiment": -1,
  "language": "Serbo-Croatian",
  "published": "2017-05-02T22:00:00.000Z",
  "country": "RS"
}

Although both records originate from the same article text, their target aspects and corresponding sentiment labels differ. The first record is positive because the article reports that Erste banka achieved its best result since entering the Serbian market. The second record is negative because Telenor banka is discussed as repeating a weak business result. This illustrates why the task is formulated as document-level entity-targeted sentiment analysis: sentiment is predicted with respect to a specific target entity rather than assigned broadly to the document as a whole.

The same training and validation pool is supplied under three splits. Therefore, the four partition files contain 223,328 record entries in total. This is not the number of distinct records. The target catalogue contains 65 targets and no dataset records.

Files in the submitted archive:

- hbs_train_val_0.json, hbs_train_val_1.json, and hbs_train_val_2.json: the three random train and validation splits of the same 70,307-record pool.
- hbs_test.json: the held-out test set with 12,407 records.
- hbs_aspects.json: the 65 targets, their forms, and keyword patterns. Use this file to identify seen and unseen targets when calculating Macro-F1, quadratic weighted kappa, or other scores.
- statistics.json: exact counts for records, articles, labels, languages, characters, and tokens.
- hbs-dataloader.ipynb: examples for loading and inspecting the data, displaying sentiment-label tables by target, and tallying seen, unseen, and train/validation-only targets.
- README.md: the dataset description, file guide, record-field guide, and usage examples.
- CITATION.cff: structured citation information, including the Frontiers article, GitHub repository, and Hugging Face model collection.
- LICENSE-and-access.md: a plain-language summary of the access conditions.
- release-validation.json: the machine-readable report of the schema, split, target-catalogue, and tag checks.
- MANIFEST.sha256: SHA-256 checksums for all files in the archive.

dc.description:
MEZZANINE-NstdLex is a dataset containing 4,281 potentially non-standard vocabulary candidates from the Sloleks Morphological Lexicon of Slovene (collected from among the manually inspected entries of version 3.0; http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1745) and various corpora of spoken Slovene (e.g. GOS 1.1 http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1438; GOS-VL 4.2 http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1444; Artur 1.0 http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1772) and transcriptions (not publicly available) of Slovene university lectures used for the Online Notes project (https://www.cjvt.si/online-notes/).

Most of the candidates were collected through manual analysis, with the exception of 1,232 candidate pairs in file "MEZZANINE-NstdLex__Sloleks3.0_levenshtein.tsv", which were extracted automatically by comparing pairs of entries using Levenshtein distance to extract potential non-standard pairs that differ in the presence of the letter "j" (e.g. "genialec" vs. "genijalec").

The candidates were manually annotated in terms of their non-standardness according to a custom typology (STD - standard vocabulary, NST - vocabulary that is non-standard in terms of register, OBL - vocabulary that is non-standard in terms of form, NSTg - vocabulary that is non-standard and typically spoken; combinations of these tags are also possible for borderline examples).

The main purpose of the dataset is to provide an overview of different types of non-standard and spoken words in Slovene. The overview can be used as a basis for a robust, empirical development of lexicographic labels for Slovene language resources.

In version 1.1, a total of 44 additional manually identified candidates were added in "MEZZANINE-NstdLex__Sloleks3.0_manual.tsv", and several missing or erroneous tags were updated in "MEZZANINE-NstdLex__Sloleks3.0_levenshtein.tsv".

For more information on the structure of the dataset, please consult 00README.txt.

dc.description:
WAX-sl is the first Slovenian word association dataset that pairs cue–association pairs with a short explanatory sentence and, for a subset of the data, a semantic relation label. It adapts the methodology of the English WAX (Word Association eXplanations) dataset (Liu et al., 2022) to Slovenian.

The 100 cue words were randomly sampled from the Reference List of Slovenian Frequent Common Words (Arhar Holdt et al., 2020), balanced by part of speech (34 nouns, 33 verbs, 33 adjectives). Data were elicited in two phases from 9 paid annotators (students of linguistics/digital linguistics), each cue answered by 4 participants: in Phase 1 participants gave up to three free associations per cue, and in Phase 2 they wrote a short sentence (3–15 words) explaining the relation between cue and association. This produced 1,261 cue–association–explanation triples.

A subset of 700 triples (covering all 100 cues) was further annotated with a semantic relation label using an extended version of the WAX relation taxonomy, comprising 21 fine-grained labels across five coarse categories (Concept-Properties, Situational, Taxonomic, Linguistic, None-of-the-Above). Each item was independently labelled by two of five trained annotators and adjudicated by a third curator; inter-annotator agreement (pairwise Cohen's κ) was 0.46. The remaining 561 triples were not selected for relation annotation and are marked NA in the Relation column.

The dataset is released as a CSV file with the columns: ID (unique triple identifier), CUE (cue word), ASSOCIATION (association given in response to the cue), EXPLANATION (explanatory sentence linking cue and association), and RELATION (semantic relation label, or NA if not annotated).

WAX-sl was created as part of the master's thesis "A multilingual comparison of human-generated and LLM-generated associations" (Vrabl, 2026), which also compares this human dataset against associations generated by three LLMs (Gemma 3, GaMS, Magistral Small).

dc.description:
The Trendi corpus is a monitor corpus of Slovenian. It contains news articles from 106 media websites, published by 64 publishers. Trendi 2026-07 covers the period from January 2019 to August 2026, complementing the Gigafida 2.2 reference corpus of written Slovene (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/2106).

The contents of the Trendi corpus are obtained using the Jožef Stefan Institute Newsfeed service (http://newsfeed.ijs.si/). The texts have been annotated using the CLASSLA-Stanza pipeline (https://github.com/clarinsi/classla), including syntactic parsing according to the Universal Dependencies (https://universaldependencies.org/sl/) and Named Entities (https://nl.ijs.si/janes/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/SlovenianNER-eng-v1.1.pdf).

An important addition are topics or thematical categories, which have been automatically assigned to each text. There are 13 categories altogether: Arts and culture, Crime and accidents, Economy, Environment, Health, Leisure, Politics and Law, Science and Technology, Society, Sports, Weather, Entertainment, and Education. The text classification uses the following models: Text classification model SloBERTa-Trendi-Topics 1.0 (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1709), Text classification model fastText-Trendi-Topics 1.0 (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1710), and the SloBERTa model (https://huggingface.co/cjvt/sloberta-trendi-topics).

The corpus is currently not available as a downloadable dataset due to copyright restrictions but we hope to make at least some of it available in the near future. The corpus is accessible through CLARIN.SI concordancers. If you would like to use the dataset for research purposes, please contact Iztok Kosem (iztok.kosem@ijs.si).

At the time, he was studying political economy; he was particularly interested in how the stock market and the circulation of capital functioned. Using the North American meat-processing industry as an example, he demonstrated how investors speculate, deliberately creating surpluses or shortages, thereby influencing the price movements of raw materials and products, stimulating or curbing production, and consequently affecting the price of labor and the unemployment rate. Another important dimension of the play is that Brecht introduces the church—represented by Ivana, the leader of a religious sect and his variation on the motif of the Maid of Orleans—into this market-driven slaughter orchestrated by various investors and speculators. Brecht’s Ivana takes on the role of a mediator between capitalists and workers with the aim of restarting the investment cycle, which alone can (at least temporarily) pull the capitalist machine out of the mud. At the same time, the church participates in the circulation of capital, as the industry’s largest capitalist allocates a portion of his profits to it.

Buffalo Bill, the creator of this grand spectacle—which was seen by 60 million spectators over the course of 20 years—can in fact be considered the inventor of mass entertainment or spectacle, the first “reality show.” The Wild West Show featured real Native Americans, whom Buffalo Bill may have thus saved from the genocide that was still taking place in the U.S. at the time. Alongside them were real cowboys, who had once actually fought against them. Through a series of adaptations and distortions of (uncomfortable) historical facts, the actual genocide of Native Americans was transformed on stage into a profitable spectacle that, through the power of the simulacrum, created a new “truth” and a reworked or entirely fictionalized image of the Native American. These stereotypes were later carried over into Westerns without any critical distance. With his incisive writing, Éric Vuillard, on the one hand, reveals the workings of the emerging society of the spectacle, and on the other, dismantles the heroic legend of the founding of the United States, behind which lie greed and cruel ruthlessness.

Social issues are not overlooked either—including the famous Maribor protests—even though Sedmak, a lucid critic of the oversaturation caused by media-constructed reality, deliberately eschews a regular chronicle of social events, reasoning that there are already enough other "opinion-stirrers" out there. In this respect, too, this "anarchistic lover of coincidences"—rather than... ...someone who sought career connections, a vitalist who never felt the need to defeat anyone in sports just to feel good about himself—a unique individual. In its pages, the author firmly establishes himself as a broad-minded, witty, playful, and aphoristically gifted figure—a passionate, perceptive observer and thinker who is honest with both himself and others. Borut Gombač. Magazine publications were followed by debut books, yet Borut Gombač persisted with magazine contributions—though even these became increasingly rare. It seemed the poet had found other literary genres to test his gift: prose, children's literature, and radio drama. Those of us following him only from afar had no inkling that his highly distinctive and compelling poetic voice had not fallen silent for even a moment. I imagine how, over the years, his drawer filled with poems, yet the poet’s hands were exacting when it came to selecting and evaluating the texts. Just as exacting is his pen, which touches the whiteness of the paper with great restraint, rarely leaving a mark. Poems are made of words; thus, every single word must be questioned, examined, and tested on the tongue a hundred times over before it is permitted—and able—to take its place in the sequence of other words. That is why Gombač’s poems are so sparing with words, and why the collection "Razblinjene dlani" (Dissolved palms) contains so much white space and so few poems. But—what poems they are!

The collection "Priveži dušo na moj haiku" (Tether your soul to my haiku) is a cycle of contemporary haikus that capture nature, the passage of time, and solitude in fleeting moments. The lyrical voice observes the world suspended between silence and convulsion: from blossoming to decay, from play to death. Nature (an owl, a birch tree, rain, snow) becomes a mirror of inner states, while the language remains condensed, fragmentary, and evocatively meditative. dc.description:
The Trendi corpus is a monitor corpus of Slovenian. It contains news articles from 106 media websites, published by 64 publishers. Trendi 2026-09 covers the period from January 2019 to September 2026, complementing the Gigafida 2.2 reference corpus of written Slovene (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/2106).

The contents of the Trendi corpus are obtained using the Jožef Stefan Institute Newsfeed service (http://newsfeed.ijs.si/). The texts have been annotated using the CLASSLA-Stanza pipeline (https://github.com/clarinsi/classla), including syntactic parsing according to the Universal Dependencies (https://universaldependencies.org/sl/) and Named Entities (https://nl.ijs.si/janes/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/SlovenianNER-eng-v1.1.pdf).

An important addition are topics or thematical categories, which have been automatically assigned to each text. There are 13 categories altogether: Arts and culture, Crime and accidents, Economy, Environment, Health, Leisure, Politics and Law, Science and Technology, Society, Sports, Weather, Entertainment, and Education. The text classification uses the following models: Text classification model SloBERTa-Trendi-Topics 1.0 (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1709), Text classification model fastText-Trendi-Topics 1.0 (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/1710), and the SloBERTa model (https://huggingface.co/cjvt/sloberta-trendi-topics).

The corpus is currently not available as a downloadable dataset due to copyright restrictions but we hope to make at least some of it available in the near future. The corpus is accessible through CLARIN.SI concordancers. If you would like to use the dataset for research purposes, please contact Iztok Kosem (iztok.kosem@ijs.si).
